findings.location: AD-7 lines 334-348 and test strategy line 461; contracts/chat-provider-streaming-v1.md lines 18-32; compare spec.md FR-054 lines 253-255, Provider Stream definition line 267, and SC-015 line 292
findings.evidence: The accepted specification requires each provider chunk to be at most 16 KiB and the complete assembled response to be at most 64 KiB measured as received bytes. The corrected plan explicitly redefines FR-054's Provider Chunk as a decoded content delta after JSON unescape/re-encoding and counts only those decoded answer bytes toward 16,384/65,536 acceptance, while permitting one raw SSE line/event up to 131,072 wire bytes and a raw body up to 1,048,576 bytes. An escape-heavy or metadata-heavy received event can therefore exceed the accepted 16 KiB received-byte requirement and still produce a release-accepted decoded delta. This is not merely an implementation safety-cap choice: it changes the normative measurement domain and could let Tier 1/Tier 3 claim SC-015 while violating the unchanged specification.
findings.correction_outcome: Keep raw reads, SSE framing, decoded deltas, and final answer domains distinct, but make the plan and contracts conform to the accepted received-byte limits: name the exact received logical provider-chunk boundary, enforce its 16,384-byte cap before decoding, enforce the accepted 65,536-byte assembled received-response domain, retain any stricter decoded-answer limits as separate additional bounds, and add exact/+1 plus escape-heavy vectors that prove both received and decoded counters. If post-unescape decoded bytes are instead the intended normative product requirement, return to the specification owner and revise FR-054/SC-015 explicitly before planning; do not silently reinterpret them in the plan.
